statement: Fix a deterministic nearest-neighbor environment on Z^d with strictly positive transition probabilities, and a nonzero direction l. Put A_l={lim_n X_n dot l=+infinity} and q(x)=P_x^omega(A_l). If inf_{x in Z^d} q(x)>0, then q(x)=1 for every x.
assumptions: time-homogeneous Markov chain in a fixed environment
A_l is invariant under removal of any finite path prefix
proof_or_counterexample: P_x^omega(A_l|F_n)=q(X_n). The bounded martingale converges to 1_{A_l} by Levy's upward theorem. Its positive lower bound excludes convergence to zero, so P_x^omega(A_l)=1.
remaining_gap: General iid strict ellipticity has not been shown to supply a positive quenched spatial infimum.
review_status: one scoped mathematical KEEP; cross-login and response-side served-model gate unverified

statement: For a fixed elliptic nearest-neighbor environment and a fixed nonzero direction, q(x)=P_x^omega(A_l) is either identically 0, identically 1, or strictly between 0 and 1 everywhere with inf_x q=0 and sup_x q=1. Uniform ellipticity only supplies the distance-dependent bound q(x)>=kappa^{|x-y|_1}q(y). Under a stationary ergodic law with 0<E[q(0)]<1 the third alternative holds almost surely.
assumptions: uniform ellipticity only for the explicit Harnack bound
stationary ergodic environment law only for the annealed assertion
proof_or_counterexample: Finite-path Markov comparison propagates positivity of q and 1-q. L1 applied to either event forces inf q=0 and sup q=1 whenever q has an interior value. Spatial ergodicity applied to the shift-invariant positivity events gives the annealed assertion.
remaining_gap: Exclude the interior alternative under iid rows; this statement does not exclude it.

statement: For every d>=2 there is an explicit uniformly elliptic deterministic nonstationary nearest-neighbor environment with 0<q(x)<1 everywhere, q(0)=3/4, inf q=0, and sup q=1. It refutes the auxiliary implication from pointwise positivity and uniform ellipticity to probability-one escape, outside the iid class.
assumptions: on x_1>=0, horizontal probabilities 3/8 and 1/8; swapped on x_1<0
environment is not stationary or iid
proof_or_counterexample: The embedded horizontal birth-death chain escapes to one of two infinities. Its exact escape profile is q(k)=1-(1/4)3^{-k} for k>=0, and q(k)=(3/4)3^k for k<=0. First-step and gambler's-ruin calculations determine q(0)=3/4.
remaining_gap: No counterexample satisfying C0044 iid assumptions is supplied or claimed.

statement: In any uniformly elliptic nearest-neighbor environment on Z^d with zero local drift projected onto a fixed nonzero l at every site, the projected walk satisfies liminf X_n dot l=-infinity and limsup X_n dot l=+infinity almost surely from every starting site. Thus P_x^omega(A_l)=P_x^omega(A_-l)=0, including any iid law supported on such rows.
assumptions: sum_e omega(x,e)(e dot l)=0 at every site
proof_or_counterexample: Bounded increments and quadratic variation floor v=2 kappa||l||_2^2 imply finite expected exit from every finite projected interval. Optional stopping bounds upper-exit probability by (a+L)/(a+b+L). Send b to infinity to force hitting each negative level; repeat for -M and countably intersect.
remaining_gap: Mixed projected drifts fall outside this subclass.

statement: In any fixed nearest-neighbor environment, if its local drift projected onto a fixed nonzero l is at least a fixed delta>0 at every site, then liminf_n (X_n dot l)/n>=delta almost surely and P_x^omega(A_l)=1. Ellipticity and iid assumptions are not required.
proof_or_counterexample: The centered projected martingale has increments bounded by 2||l||_infinity. Azuma gives the summable bound 2exp(-epsilon^2 n/(8||l||_infinity^2)). Its normalized value tends to zero, while predictable drift accumulates at least delta n.
remaining_gap: A merely nonnegative drift floor is insufficient; the zero-drift case has oscillation by L3. General mixed drifts remain open in this packet.
